holidays.name: International Plastic Bag Free Day
holidays.description: A day when people around the globe ditch single-use plastic bags and dig out their reusable totes, even the ones that have been living at the bottom of the trunk for six months.
holidays.origin: Started in 2008 by the Catalan environmental group Rezero (Zero Waste Europe network), it grew into a worldwide movement to cut plastic pollution and encourage reusable alternatives.
holidays.funFact: Bangladesh became the first country in the world to ban thin plastic shopping bags, in 2002, after they were found to clog drainage systems during floods.

holidays.name: Compliment Your Mirror Day
holidays.description: A day to look yourself in the eye and say something nice to the person staring back at you. Bonus points for a dramatic hair flip and a wink.
holidays.origin: An unofficial, feel-good observance popularized through quirky holiday calendars as a lighthearted push for self-confidence and positive self-talk.
holidays.funFact: Psychologists note that positive self-affirmations, especially when spoken aloud in front of a mirror, can help reduce stress and boost self-esteem for some people.

holidays.name: Fried Clam Day
holidays.description: A salute to the crispy, golden, gloriously messy fried clam, best eaten from a paper tray at a seaside shack with tartar sauce on everything.
holidays.origin: Fried clams are credited to Lawrence 'Chubby' Woodman of Essex, Massachusetts, who reportedly fried the first batch on July 3, 1916, at his roadside stand, so the day honors that moment of culinary history.
holidays.funFact: Essex, Massachusetts still celebrates itself as the birthplace of the fried clam, and Woodman's restaurant is still serving them over a century later.

holidays.name: Disobedience Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to politely, or not so politely, breaking the rules and questioning the status quo. Think of it as permission to color outside the lines, metaphorically speaking.
holidays.origin: A quirky unofficial observance that encourages people to think about the value of civil disobedience and challenging authority, tying into the spirit of independence that surrounds the days leading up to July 4th.
holidays.funFact: Henry David Thoreau's 1849 essay 'Civil Disobedience' went on to influence leaders like Mahatma Gandhi and Martin Luther King Jr.

holidays.name: Dog Days of Summer Begin
holidays.description: The traditional start of the hottest, laziest, most sweltering stretch of summer, when everyone and every pooch is justified in lying motionless in front of a fan.
holidays.origin: The ancient Greeks and Romans linked the period to the rising of Sirius, the 'Dog Star,' alongside the sun. The traditional dates run from July 3 to August 11.
holidays.funFact: The Romans believed the heat from Sirius combined with the sun's heat caused fevers and bad luck, and they sometimes sacrificed a brown dog at the start of the period to appease the star's rage.
